web_evidence.title: Stephen King on How He Wrote His Latest Novel
web_evidence.note: The author interview explicitly distinguishes the novel’s third-person story from Billy’s extensively developed written life story and discusses scenes and long material from that autobiography.

web_evidence.title: Billy Summers Summary and Study Guide

person_note: The novel has a sustained third-person-present outer narrative centered on Billy and recurring first-person autobiographical material written first by Billy and ultimately continued by Alice. The first-person material is interspersed, substantial, and expands into the late story rather than being an isolated speech or document, so the methodology’s third-person-frame plus sustained first-person-story rule yields ALTERNATING. The quote set independently contains many outer third-person scenes and several participating first-person manuscript passages. Some popular quotations are clipped and their precise Billy-versus-Alice authorship is uncertain, but that uncertainty does not affect the demonstrated alternation of narrative person.
